They are not protocol ERROR messages and carry no wave terminal or lifecycle semantics" (lines 2-5).

The return type is a readonly view of two mutable local arrays, so callers cannot mutate through the declared type while the function itself never writes to the caller's array or to any result object.

Failure never travels as protocol ERROR." So an error payload by itself does not send a protocol ERROR message, does not end a graph run, and does not authorize automatic retry. Likewise retryable?: boolean (packages/ts/src/data/index.ts:19) is only an optional hint field on an issue; it is not consulted by this collector and grants no retry authority. Lifecycle readiness observations such as runEndReady are "current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred" (README.md:144).
